Done
I hit the tool-use ceiling mid-build, so this response is a findings report rather than the archive. Everything below is verified against dump.txt — no guesses.

The build error: found, one line, one cause
tests/MyRestaurant.EndToEnd.Tests/Harness/TableOrderJourneys.cs, in LineOffersRemovalAsync. The compiler points at line 412 (the method's opening brace, which is where CS4007 is always reported), but the offending code is at line 433:

csharp
throw new InvalidOperationException(
    string.Create(
        CultureInfo.InvariantCulture,
        $"There is no committed line for '{menuItemName}' on this order."
        + $" It holds: {Describe(await ReadCommittedLinesAsync(page))}."));
The await sits inside an interpolation hole of a string that binds to DefaultInterpolatedStringHandler (a ref struct), which cannot survive the await. The fix is the pattern this file already uses in four other places — hoist the read into a local first:

csharp
string committed = Describe(await ReadCommittedLinesAsync(page));

throw new InvalidOperationException(
    string.Create(
        CultureInfo.InvariantCulture,
        $"There is no committed line for '{menuItemName}' on this order."
        + $" It holds: {committed}."));
I scanned all 317 files for await inside interpolation holes: this is the only occurrence in the repository.

"Some tests are now failing" — they aren't
claude-terminal.txt shows dotnet test at 956 total / 0 failed. Slice 9's note put the total at 971. The 15-test gap is exactly the E2E project, which never ran because it didn't compile. Fix CS4007 and you're back at 971/0. Nothing else is red.

One stale reference worth fixing while I'm in the file
KitchenJourneys.cs:271 has <see cref="TableOrderJourneys.BasketWarningCountAsync"/> — that method doesn't exist (it became ReadBasketAsync / BasketContents.UnavailableMarks). It's silent today only because GenerateDocumentationFile is false; it would be CS1574 under CI's TreatWarningsAsErrors if doc generation were ever switched on.

The next step, scoped and ready to write
M6 Slice 11 — §16.3 scenario 8 ("a send sits unfulfilled 60 s → exactly one reminder alert"). I traced the whole path:

KitchenReminderService.ScanInterval is a fixed 5 s; the threshold is KITCHEN_SUBMISSION_REMINDER_SECONDS, floor 1, default 60. The harness hard-codes "60" in RestaurantInstance.CreateProcess, so it needs the same parameterisation TABLE_JOIN_TOKEN_ROTATION_SECONDS already has — through RestaurantHarness.StartInstanceAsync and RestaurantInstance.StartAsync. At 5 s the reminder lands within 10 s of the send instead of 65.
Adding a second int parameter breaks three positional call sites (StartInstanceAsync(BoundaryWatchingRotationSeconds, cancellationToken) at lines 119, 194, 349) — as compile errors, not silently. They become named arguments.
The board publishes data-unseen-alerts but not the reminder count; reminder-ness exists only as " (1 overdue)" inside the badge. One additive attribute, data-unseen-reminders="@_alerts.UnseenReminderCount", is the same move as Slice 9's .order-party-line-name and Slice 10's .order-prune-notice.
KitchenBoardSnapshot gains UnseenReminderCount — only two construction sites, both inside KitchenJourneys.
"Exactly one" is best proven by acknowledging the badge and then watching several scans go by in silence, plus reading kitchen_notification grouped by kind (the UNIQUE (order_event_identifier, kind) row is the actual guarantee).
